protocol_checks.vulnerability_mechanism: Confirmed. CVE-2026-31976 is PUBLISHED and GHSA-f8q5-h5qh-33mh is not withdrawn. The vulnerability was mutable-tag poisoning: v5 was moved to unmerged PR #48 commit 4bf1d4e19ad81a3e8d4063755ae0f482dd3baf12, whose injected action.yml step registered the runner with 91.214.78.178, polled for commands, eval'd them, and exfiltrated results.
protocol_checks.atomic_bic: Confirmed as 4bf1d4e19ad81a3e8d4063755ae0f482dd3baf12 for the published tag-delivery event. The advisory and contemporaneous StepSecurity capture identify that exact single commit as the object served by v5; it added the implant to the clean v5.38.1 base. The identical PR #46 and #47 commits were separate failed delivery attempts, not ancestors or members of the delivered PR #48 commit.
protocol_checks.immediate_parent_absence: Confirmed with an evidence-boundary caveat. The contemporaneous commit capture identifies one parent, ea66a5ad3128270e853f46013be382e761d930b9. That surviving parent resolves to v5.38.1, and its action.yml goes directly from scanner installation to scanner execution with no telemetry step, C2 address, nip.io host, or eval loop. The BIC object itself has since been garbage-collected and cannot be cat-file'd again.
protocol_checks.squash_member_decomposition: Confirmed not applicable. 4bf1d4e is represented as a one-parent first-write commit, not a squash aggregate, merge, refactor, move, or revert. The other two malicious SHAs were independent PR attempts with the same payload, so there is no finer public member to decompose from 4bf1d4e.
protocol_checks.affected_and_fixed_release_membership: Confirmed. Public incident evidence records v5 pointing to 4bf1d4e during the affected March 3-10 window. Current refs show signed v5 peeled to clean ea66a5ad3128270e853f46013be382e761d930b9, while v6 and v6.4.0 point to clean 13c6ed2797df7d85749864e2cbcf09c893f43b23; the v6.4.0 action.yml contains no implant.
protocol_checks.direct_fix_or_unpatched_state: Correction required. 13c6ed2797df7d85749864e2cbcf09c893f43b23 is a safe v6.4.0 pin target and README guidance commit, not the direct remediation: v6.4.0 was published March 9 while poisoned v5 remained live. The direct fix was deletion of v5 on March 10, followed later by a signed safe retag, so no direct-fix commit SHA exists.
protocol_checks.bic_only_ai_attribution: Confirmed NOT_AI. BIC attribution is confined to 4bf1d4e: contemporaneous evidence identifies the author as the compromised xygeni-onboarding-app-dev[bot] credential and the incident as deliberate attacker malware, with no BIC AI marker. The Claude Opus 4.6 trailer belongs only to later commit 13c6ed2 and cannot be projected backward onto the BIC.
protocol_checks.advisory_disposition: Confirmed real vulnerability, not FALSE_POSITIVE: CVE.org state is PUBLISHED and the reviewed GHSA has withdrawn_at=null.

findings: The primary correctly identifies the tag-poisoning mechanism, delivered BIC 4bf1d4e19ad81a3e8d4063755ae0f482dd3baf12, clean immediate parent ea66a5ad3128270e853f46013be382e761d930b9, and NOT_AI attribution.

The primary incorrectly sets direct_fix_sha to 13c6ed2797df7d85749864e2cbcf09c893f43b23. That commit changed README pinning guidance and points at a clean v6.4.0 release, but it did not remove or retarget poisoned v5; direct remediation was a Git ref deletion on March 10.

The current clone and remote no longer expose PR #46/#47/#48 refs or their three malicious commit objects; issue #56 records GitHub Support ticket #4207039 deleting the refs and garbage-collecting those objects.
remaining_gap: The raw 4bf1d4e commit object and message bytes are no longer retrievable after GitHub Support garbage collection. Its parent, diff, author display, and tag association therefore depend on the contemporaneous commit-page capture plus advisory/vendor records, although the surviving parent tree and current safe refs remain independently reproducible.
